evidence: advance-order-use-case.ts and list-orders-use-case.ts both validate status with the shared domain function isOrderStatus. The rule is called from one place, not copied.
Order-returning use cases (AdvanceOrderUseCase, CancelOrderUseCase, ListOrdersUseCase, PlaceOrderUseCase) all build DTOs with the shared toOrderDto from order-mapper.ts.
Persistence is reached only through injected ports: OrderRepository (findById, findByStatus, save, nextId) and ProductRepository.findAll. No direct database or ORM client is used.
CancelOrderUseCase and PlaceOrderUseCase delegate stock changes to the domain StockAllocationService (release/reserve). They do not change product quantities themselves.
get-stock-levels-use-case.ts maps products inline to StockLevelDto, which is declared in order-dto.ts. No product mapper exists, so nothing is bypassed.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The src/application module passes. It holds the application use cases for the order/stock bounded context, the DTOs they return and an order mapper. Every use case reaches persistence only through the domain repository ports (OrderRepository, ProductRepository) or the StockAllocationService. None uses a database, ORM or query client directly.

All four order use cases build their output with the shared toOrderDto mapper rather than mapping inline. Status validation in AdvanceOrderUseCase and ListOrdersUseCase calls the one shared isOrderStatus definition from the domain, so the rule is not copied. Only the error messages differ.

Two use cases repeat a small 'findById or throw NOT_FOUND' guard. This is a short lookup step at the application level, not a business rule or invariant written out twice, so it does not reach the rubric's bar for duplication.

GetStockLevelsUseCase maps products to StockLevelDto inline. No product mapper exists in the module, so it bypasses nothing. Placing StockLevelDto in order-dto.ts is a small naming quirk, not a split into unrelated concerns: stock reservation and release are part of the same ordering flow.
